name: Drevsin Tamarind-Pomelo Sour Ribbons
manufacturer: Drevsin Candy Works (street brand, the Gray Zone-adjacent)
description: Long synth-gummy ribbons coated in crystallized tamarind-pomelo sour sugar. Aggressively tart, cheap, and sold in bulk from open bins at the Gray Zone market stalls.
flavor_profile: Immediate face-puckering sourness from tamarind acid and pomelo pith bitterness; the sour sugar coating dissolves into a sweeter, fruitier chew beneath; faint salty finish
price: Φ0.25 per ribbon, Φ1.80 for a bag of 10
slogan: More sour than you want. Exactly what you need.
cultural_context: A childhood staple for anyone who grew up in the Gray Zone. The open-bin format means they're unpackaged and cheap — a sign of their tier. Tier 3 adults sometimes buy them as nostalgia, slightly embarrassed at the counter. The sourness is a point of pride.
story_hooks: A batch of ribbons is making kids sick — the sour coating is cut with an industrial acidulant not approved for consumption
The Drevsin family operation is one of the last unfranchised candy makers in the Gray Zone; a corponation buyout offer has just arrived with an implicit threat attached
Someone is using the bulk bins to pass contraband — small items wrapped and coated to look like candy
